review_text:
Counter-Strike 2 to godny następca CS:GO. Gra zachowuje klasyczny, wymagający gameplay, który od lat definiuje gatunek FPS, ale jednocześnie wprowadza świeżość dzięki silnikowi Source 2.

Największy plus to poprawiona grafika – mapy wyglądają nowocześniej, oświetlenie jest bardziej realistyczne, a efekty dymu (smoke) zmieniają sposób rozgrywki i dodają taktycznej głębi. Strzelanie nadal jest satysfakcjonujące i wymaga precyzji oraz dobrej kontroli recoila.

Na minus można zaliczyć problemy techniczne, które pojawiały się po premierze – sporadyczne bugi, matchmaking czy balans niektórych aspektów gry. Jednak twórcy regularnie aktualizują tytuł i wprowadzają poprawki.

Podsumowując: jeśli lubisz rywalizacyjne FPS-y i klimat klasycznego Counter-Strike’a, CS2 to obowiązkowa pozycja. Gra wymaga cierpliwości i nauki, ale daje ogromną satysfakcję z wygranych meczów.

review_text:
Apex Legends used to be an incredible game—especially around 2020 and the years that followed. The movement, the gunplay, the characters, the pacing… it all came together in a way that made it one of the most exciting battle royales out there. It was even the game that kicked off my streaming journey, so I’ll always have a soft spot for it.

But somewhere along the way, the magic faded. Instead of focusing on long‑standing bugs or quality‑of‑life fixes, the developers kept pumping out new content, reworking characters that didn’t need to be touched, and releasing new legends that felt overpowered right out of the gate. The balance issues piled up, and the game slowly shifted from fun and competitive to sweaty and exhausting.

These days, the lobbies feel dominated by players who treat every match like a tournament, and that casual, chaotic fun the game used to have just isn’t there anymore. The core of what made Apex special is buried under layers of imbalance and design choices that never quite landed.

I’ll always appreciate what the game meant to me, but it doesn’t feel the same—and at this point, it probably never will.

review_text: I love a lot of what Apex Legends has to offer. The gun play is one of the best in any game I have ever played and the charachters are very fun. However I can’t recommend the game strictly on the monetization. For example before this new season (24) there were leaked mini battle passes for all of the new legends that would add a ton of progression that was desperately needed. It would have given the players something worth playing for. But what does EA do? Make you pay 10$ for each one. This isn’t even mentioning the collection events that cost 300+ dollars to complete. They also just added a new mobile game pay system that makes you pay to unlock something cheap and then to unlock something free. All the skins are also egregiously overpriced in general. It’s all there to just make you spend as much money as possible it’s trash. They don’t really care about the players they care about the money that’s it. The balance changes are often mediocre and  don’t always fix all the problems they should. EA is lucky the foundation of this game is as good as it is otherwise people wouldn’t put up with the gross monetization. If your a new player that know you won’t buy anything then maybe give it a try. Otherwise steer clear it’s not worth your time until EA gets it together and starts to care more about the player base.(which will never happen)

It’s 20 minutes of looting, 5 minutes of repositioning, and 0.4 seconds of getting headshot by someone you never saw.

The gunplay? Heavy.
The recoil? Personal.
The footsteps? Louder than your heartbeat.

This isn’t slide-cancel chaos. It’s tactical, punishing, and sometimes unfair - which is exactly why winning feels insane.

This is NOT a hardware issue and NOT a software configuration problem. The problem is the game itself. PUBG runs on an outdated engine that clearly struggles with modern high-end systems and high refresh rate monitors. The game used to run much better in the past, but after recent updates the performance and smoothness have noticeably degraded.

If you’re using modern high-end hardware, don’t expect a flawless experience. The engine needs serious optimization.

review_text:
Pal world is a great game, kinda like Pokemon but with it's own thing.

In palworld your Pals are weaponized and ready for battle, they often have abilities or they can have guns. Your goal is to take down every tower with it's unique character and pal for that biome / region. Palworld is openworld (3d) and offers alot of mechanics and things to explore. 

Oh and don't even get me started on the 100% steam completion. The final towers 6 and 7 lol are really hard to fight if you play on normal difficulty then the level progression of your character can take a long time when your above level 50. Palworld can be really grindy and requires decent skill and energy to be able to fully complete the game if your not doing a baby difficulty like easy mode or a custom difficulty that makes the game really easy.

Sumary - Palworld is a grind to beat every boss. Requires alot of time and effort if your truly gonna 100% steam completion it. Palworld adds more achievements over time so your gonna have to come back to get the new ones.  Overall i do recommend Palworld if you like it or like Pokemon then purchase it, Palworld has great gameplay and great exploration,

review_text:
If you are thinking of picking up this game in the current year then understand that there is almost no fun to be had until you have enough hours/skill to competently fight against people who have been playing this game 5-10 years before you. The skill ceiling and skill gap between new and experienced players is so high that it's no exaggeration to say a new player has to sink at least ~50 hours of gameplay to reasonably hold their own in casual matches. Many new players realise this when trying this game out as they are decimated against better opponents, and end up quitting due to this. Thus the current playerbase of this game consists mostly of either new installs or aged veterans, as many quit due to the extremely harsh skill filter.

Because of this reason many games end up being steamrolls where new players are stomped by the experienced. This is not fun for either party, as newbies don't enjoy being steamrolled and experienced players looking for challenge become bored with dominating every game, while the dwindling player numbers mean that matches where both teams are of similar skill level become harder and harder to find.

If this does not bother you and you are willing to invest time to learn the mechanics of this game, then this is indeed one of the most fun games available to this day, with top-notch gameplay, artstyle, and to an extent community. However as the state of matchmaking is right now, it's hard to recommend a new player to start playing without at least a disclaimer of the insane skill gap they are likely to experience.

And if you're not a new player reading this then what the ♥♥♥♥ are you doing? You know you'll be back so why bother listening to some 1000 hour scrub whine about how fresh install timmy25 casual rank 4 ends on their team while the other team is full 6q rank 150 tier 8 9684 hour ozfortress.com PUGlords.

review_text:
Всем приветики! ~(˘▾˘~) Я просто обожаю играть в Team Fortress 2! Это самая лучшая игра для таких нежных созданий, как я! ✨🎀

Когда я захожу на сервер, все мальчики сразу обращают на меня внимание! Они такие заботливые... Солдатик всегда первый подбегает ко мне со своей ракетницей и говорит что-то про "америку", но я знаю, что на самом деле он хочет сказать "как я тебя хочу"... э... то есть "как я рад тебя видеть"! (⁄ ⁄>⁄ ▽ ⁄<⁄ ⁄)

А Шпион... Ой, он такой загадочный! Он всегда подкрадывается сзади и нежно обнимает меня своим ножичком... Иногда так неожиданно, что я даже вскрикиваю "Ай!" — но это же от счастья! Правда-правда! А потом он шепчет мне на ушко своим французским акцентом... Мур-мур~ 💕

Хеви — это просто большой пушистый мишка! Он такой сильный, такой мощный... Когда он наставляет на меня свой пулемёт, я чувствую себя такой маленькой и беззащитной... Он как будто говорит: "Никому тебя не отдам"... и никому не отдаёт! Потому что сам меня... ну... "обнимает" очень долго и крепко! Так крепко, что даже вырваться не могу, хе-хе~ (✿◠‿◠)

Медик... Ах, этот немецкий доктор... Он такой заботливый! Лечит всех, кто мной интересуется, чтобы наша "игра" продолжалась вечно! А когда я подбегаю к нему с щечками и прошу полечить, он так многозначительно смотрит на меня и говорит "Nein"... Это же по-немецки "нет"? Но я чувствую в этом "да"! Определённо "да"! 🩷

Инженер построил для меня специальный уголок на второй базе... Там такая уютная турелька! Она как ревнивая подружка — как только я захожу, сразу начинает меня "щекотать"... Везде-везде... И долго-долго... А Инженер стоит в сторонке, попивает кофе и улыбается — мол, так и надо, моя хорошая... 🥺🔧

В общем, Team Fortress 2 — это игра, где каждый найдёт себе занятие по душе! А для таких милых созданий, как я, здесь просто рай! Меня здесь все хотят, все ждут, все обо мне заботятся... Иногда даже слишком заботятся... Но я же хорошая девочка, я стерплю! Для таких заботливых мальчиков — всё что угодно! 💖

Оценка: миллион алых роз из пулемёта 🌹
Совет: заходите на сервер в юбочке — сразу почувствуете себя звездой! ✧･ﾟ: *✧･ﾟ:*

P.S. Если увидите на сервере самого милого фембойчика с ником "Nya_TF2_Girl" — не бейте сильно... Я просто хочу, чтобы меня... ну... вы поняли...

Захожу каждый вечер на 2Fort. Жду вас. Особенно сзади. 💕

review_text:
If you haven't played this game in it's over 18 years (as of me typing this review) of history, you need to give it a go. The gameplay is fun, and a lot of the weapons you can unlock are as well.

There's plenty of different game modes to try out, King of the Hill and Control Points are my favorites personally, and tons of weapons to chose from for each class. Speaking of which, each class has entertaining and funny dialogue, great personality (especially if you check out the official webcomic on the website), and while cosmetic items can be hit or miss sometimes (and the cosmetics you need to pay for, either on the Steam Market or the in-game store), there are a ton of amazing cosmetics made by either Valve or Workshop creators.

While the games balance is a bit wonky due to the game not having had a proper balance patch since 2018 (I think a balance patch would be warranted to be clear, mainly just to buff weaker weapons like the Righteous Bison or rework weapons like the Pomson), and does take an awful lot of space on your computer as a result of it being so old and thus having a ton of content thats been adding throughout the years, I still can't recommend this game enough. Between the silly interactions you can get, the taunts, the gameplay, the cosmetics, there's bound to be something for everyone in this free-to-play.

P.S. the game also has a good balance philosophy where unlockable weapons aren't strict upgrades to others (aside from the Third Degree for some reason, but it and the item its an upgrade from, the Fire Axe, are both terrible) and are instead made to compliment various playstyles.

game_name: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II
review_text:
❌ Not Recommended

Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 feels less like a sequel and more like a yearly copy-paste with a new number slapped on the box. The download size keeps getting bigger, the store gets shinier, and somehow the actual fun keeps shrinking. The last Call of Duty I played was Call of Duty: Black Ops 6, and that game actually had potential. The gunplay felt solid, it wasn’t trying to be a jetpack space opera, and for a moment it almost felt grounded again. Then it felt like that potential got tossed in the trash almost immediately in favor of bundles, seasonal resets, and “we’ll patch it later” energy.

Now BO7 jumps straight into a futuristic era again like we didn’t just spend a whole game dialing it back. We went from grounded to laser-light-show overnight. It’s tonal whiplash. Instead of refining what almost worked in BO6, it feels like the franchise hit the reset button and said, “What if we just add more?” More effects. More flash. More storage space required and more bundles!

After BO6, I absolutely cannot give BO7 a chance. I’m not signing up for another cycle of 'YO YO WE ARE SO BACK CHAT" hype trailers, 100GB updates labeled “minor,” hyper-aggressive matchmaking, and cosmetic bundles that function flawlessly while core issues wait for next season. At this point the franchise isn’t evolving — it’s just respawning with a different skin. Hard pass.

game_name: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II
review_text:
THE ONLY REVIEW YOU NEED

TLDR: Zombies is fun, the multiplayer gameplay is fun for the first week but gets boring quickly and the map design is average at best.

Zombies mode is great, good story and characters plus some fun core gameplay and stunning visuals. Only issue is that it takes about 16 hours of gameplay to max out a single augment, and there are more than 30 of them. It really sucks that this game has a bad rep because of the multiplayer and few people will experience the zombies mode.

The multiplayer is typical cod just way faster. Everyone sweats, everyone pre-fires, everyone drop shots, everyone is cracked. If you don't have a 2 millisecond reaction time, you will die. If you don't pre-fire every single corner, you will die. If you don't master the movement, you will die. If you don't hit headshots, you will die.

Since this game's player count is so low, there is a very high chance you will have 1 or more insane players on the enemy team and there is no skill based match making to save you.

There is absolutely nothing that stands out in the multiplayer. If you aren't already above average at fps games, this is not a game you can relax and play after work.

review_text:
I loved this game. Not love... "loved"
It was an amazing MMO, one of the only ones I enjoyed a LOT because I'm really not a fan of tab targeting games. I spent a lot of hours on this game just having fun and doing what i enjoyed. I got really into it, so many sleepless nights just running dungeons and grinding mats... hanging out with friends. I loved the combat and loved the story. When the new update came out i was ecstatic. So much more life and love given to the game. They went downhill as soon as they opened to consoles and reworked the entire UI, it could've been great but it just felt awkward, and then they just.. lost funding i guess? I even revisited it with the most recent update but then i was met with.. "yeah no more updates and we are gonna shut down servers in a year." It was just a kick in the balls...

Now it just feels like a waste, this game had so much going for it and so much potential but now its gone. It had such a good combat system, a great community, etc. ... but now its just... sad, i see it in my favorite tab in my steam library and i just get.. sad. I will miss it.

 I mourn the loss of a good MMO that had so much potential. Just another reason to hate amazon i guess. I don't think another MMO will come out that feels like it but i really hope one does because it was so unique and fun but the MMO genre has been really crappy lately :/

review_text:
For my experience the game was fun to play. It look colorful and unique enough in its own right. I like that it was not over complicated combat like Black Desert Online but not clucky like Blessed Unleashed. One of the big issues I did have with it was limited resources fighting other players just to level up skills. Back when the game first launch it was almost impossible to train up for skill because there were so many players. It only got better because player base died down. This was a straight obvious issue they could of fixed that i know a lot of players quit because of this. The other issues was there was just no good reliable way to make money in the game. Especially when players started leaving the game. Hard to have a player only market when there are no players.

For Amazons first game it was decently well done. But there were def changes they could have made to make the entire experience better for players. I cant see myself returning to play their last season just to not benefit from it know the game is shutting down.

So far, I haven't played it a lot (explored just a few regions), but from what I experienced it is a good game, even a very good game. It was not expensive for what it offered (esp. on discount). The world is beautifully crafted and there is a lot to explore and I found it fun to play. IMHO, it is a very good MMO.

The game received a lot of unfair negativity (like many others, btw.), what in some way results in what happens now. Also, those who played 100s or 1000s of hours and put now negative reviews writing that they do not want the game to shutdown - where is logic in that?

If there is not enough players to mainain servers, I think they could at least leave the game just as a singleplayer, openworld RPG (or let run local or independently maintained servers). I could easily be preserved that way, cheaper to maintain and still earn something allowing new players to check it out. (Though, it would not be an MMO, anymore...)

Concerning the technical aspects - over last year or so the engine was changed to use less memory, more disk I/O. It was using nearly 20GB while entering settlements, now it uses like 14GB, but it uses disk a lot more. The engine could be more adaptive in these aspects, when more memory is available (and nowdays - it usually is), it could be used more effectively (that is a problem with many games, in fact).
 
I am rarely posting reviews, but here I am giving thumbs up as it is a waste to trash such product.

review_text:
New World’s launch mechanics delivered a bold and ambitious MMO experience built around territory control, persistent combat systems, and survival-flavored progression, even if they weren’t fully polished at first.

⚔️ Combat & Action Mechanics

At release, New World’s combat was real-time, responsive, and stamina-driven — closer to action RPGs than many tab-target MMOs. Dodging, blocking, and directional attacks mattered. Each weapon had a distinct rhythm: rapiers rewarded spacing and counters, great axes leaned into heavy hits and crowd control, and muskets/warbows emphasized positioning and aim. Blocking wasn’t just a numeric reduction — it mechanically stopped momentum and opened counter windows.

Weapon mastery wasn’t surface-level either. Abilities on each weapon had meaningful cooldowns and distinct mechanics (e.g., area denial with fire staves, knockdowns with void gauntlets), forcing you to pick loadouts based on tactic, not just DPS.

🛡️ Stamina & Resource Pulse

Stamina was a core mechanical meter, not a cosmetic bar. Sprinting, dodging, blocking, and heavy attacks all drained stamina, and running out in a fight wasn’t just an inconvenience — it mechanically prevented actions, forcing you to retreat or reposition. This made movement and timing as crucial as gear score in fights.

🌍 Open-World Systems & Progression

New World’s open world wasn’t a backdrop — it was a persistent mechanical ecology. Resources respawned predictably, nodes regenerated, and resource gathering (logging, mining, harvesting) unlocked crafting tiers that mechanically affected gear strength. Crafting wasn’t icing — it was a core progression loop: refine → craft → equip → repeat.

Leveling was equipment-integrated. Gear score mattered mechanically, not just numerically. Better gear unlocked higher thresholds in elite zones and defended territory bonuses more effectively.

🏙️ Territory & Faction Control

The territory control system was a standout mechanic at launch. Factions vied for control of settlements, and war sieges were large-scale mechanical events. Controlling a territory provided bonuses — tax cuts, resource yields, crafting perks — that weren’t cosmetic. These mechanics tied social strategy directly into gameplay systems, making guild organization, zoning, and contribution meaningful.

Outpost Rush, the flagship PvP mode, was built around objective mechanics rather than pure deathmatching. Control points, scoring loops, reinforcement summoning, and push mechanics made it feel like a dynamic battlefield machine rather than repetitive skirmishing.

🧍 Survival & Lifestyle Loops

At launch, food, consumables, and gear degradation had mechanical impact. Eating food provided stat buffs that mattered in combat and crafting loops; failing to repair gear meant mechanically weaker performance in fights. These systems reinforced engagement rather than being fluff.

⚙️ Rough Edges (At Launch)

While many systems were mechanically rich, they weren’t fully polished on day one. Combat could feel floaty at times, encounter pacing uneven, and some resource loops weren’t fully balanced. But mechanically, the design intent was clear: systems should interlock, not exist in isolation.

9/10 — robust action combat, territory mechanics, and progression loops that made the early MMO experience feel fresh and meaningful.

review_text:
Y'know... I really don't want to give this game a thumbs down 'cause the devs clearly put a lot of time & effort into this game but... that shouldn't be the excuse for them to insult the players 'cause why do these bosses have to be so dang difficult? And by the way y'all, that's kinda what this game is. It's centered around the bosses. Like 24/7, you're just gonna be fighting boss after boss, learning their moves over & over again and it is just sooo boring. Now, you may say, "Oh but you recommend cuphead and that game has tons of hard bosses." Okay for number 1, they're not as hard as the bosses in this game. And for #2, it has less bosses than this one.

And also... Cuphead looks a lot better than this game like say what y'all want about the graphics but... I really don't think they hold up with the high system requirements like is this where we are on the videogame evolution? Like seriously, Gears of War is an extremely good looking 360 game, Plants vs Zombies Garden Warfare 2 still holds up and yet years later we got games like this that have ugly hair & water physics while requiring NASA computers to properly run. All because people want to develop with this awful unreal engine 5 for some reason like what the heck are we doing?

Also, another thing I'm confused with this game is that... why are we only able to have better strength & defense when we craft new weapon & armor? Now for those who have the wrong idea, this isn't like some Swords & Souls kinda deal, these weapons & armor have these bonus stats like... "ohhh this staff increases your light damage" orrr "this armor increases your stamina", y'know that kind of deal. But the problem is, in order to increase your attack & defense, you need to craft a brand new weapon & armor and equip them. Even if you don't like their bonus stats. And it's like dang devs, we can't freaking have preferences now? Like y'all wanna punish us for wanting to use a certain staff & armor? They don't even allow you to upgrade them like they want you to use a brand new weapon & armor every now & then to pull the excuse of how they spiced this game up a bit. Like where is the respect?

And also, speaking of balancing, why is immobilize the only good spell? Like what's up with devs doing this thing where the 1st cool thing a character gets is the best thing when compared to the rest like why do devs do that? Heck, they even did it again with that huge guy holding some beads. Like literally the best spirit in the game, especially since he gives you a passive bonus of better defense. And that is most definitely needed 'cause learning these bosses takes time, alright?

And more on defense... say what y'all want about perfect dodging but I highly believe the window for it needs to be increased. Like I know we were made in God's image but that does not mean we are Him, alright? And on top of that, we got freaking input lag so why did y'all made the perfect dodging window so small? Now I know people are gonna say some, "git gud" or whatever but gosh dang man, what, people can't relax? Like we have to treat this like our 2nd job? Fighting the same boss over & over until we memorized their moves so we don't take crazy damage from them? Meanwhile we hit them with a literal stick? And also, I'm past the freaking ice dragon part, which is past that extremely annoying sand rat with his lame tornado and I did that in 10 hours. So don't tell me some, "git gud".

But yeah all in all, I really am saddened to give this game a thumbs down 'cause obviously the art & sound direction were on the right path (excluding the 3D graphics obviously). But considering the fact that the gameplay is freaking cancer and you need a strong PC to even run the dang thing like I think they were better off not even making this. "Oh but you're good at the game, how could you not like it?" Yes I may be good at the game. Like I am able to learn bosses and take them down but, that doesn't really mean I enjoy doing it. It feels like a chore to do. And the fact that I gotta do this for a dozen more bosses when I don't really get a good reward from them like why would I continue this? "Oh you do it for the story!"

...

Yeah okay man. I'm out.

The combat can feel a bit clunky, but for the most part I am really enjoy it. The game utilizes invisible borders a lot which simplifies getting from obj to obj. The boss fights are what I like the most and their are plenty of them.

review_text:
Again, I wish there was a middle option.

The game has so much potential but it didn't manage to grab me, but I know other people will love it. Journey to the West is a great story and the devs capture the essence of the things I love most about Chinese culture with the journal entries and the characters. 

But the combat and the linearity of a souls-like comes back to undermine the narrative. Combat feels too light and weightless, I'm never quite sure if I'm dodging and attack, and the heavy attack feels wrong.

The linearity is forgiveable but as an Elden Ring fan, I find being boxed into a set path boring and unchallenging with the pacing dictated by the devs personal opinion on the game flow, rather than mine. Elden Ring, was like Gothic and Risen with brutal difficulty curves but with a Souls respawn instead of reloading an old save.

I would strongly recommend anyone who loves Souls games and wants to be like Monkey from the 80's show.

review_text:
As hyped as I was with this one, after beating it I can say that it has a lot of good stuff, but if I could travel to the past, I'd totally spare myself the trouble and frustration.

For reference, I've beat and enjoyed Dark Souls 3, Sekiro, the 2 modern God of Wars, Stellar Blade, and other similar games. They all had difficult moments and bosses, but none of them made me feel the frustration I've felt with this one. With those, each failure meant some learning about what I did wrong and how to improve. Here, though, the sheer amount of cheep bullsh*t the bosses can throw at you is insane. This, added to the lack of responsivity of the main character means that part of the times I died I didn't feel like it was my fault, and that's the worst it can happen with this kind of games. Difficulty needs to be FAIR, and there were lots of times where it didn't feel so.


[h2] Cool Stuff [/h2]
+ Lots of beautiful environments.
+ Really liked the start of the game. Very good use of camera in cinematics throughout the game.
+ Lots of bosses. A lot of them very different, cool-looking and with epic moments.
+ Lots of side content too.
+ The cinematics at the end of chapters were very cool and different.
+ Every enemy has some story and an "ancient looking" drawing in the codex. Lots of details and production value in general.
+ Checkpoints are well placed, and even though there are multi-phased bosses, you don't have to retry from the beginning.


[h2] Not so Cool Stuff [/h2]
- The main character's lack of responsivity. The dodge has some delay, ok, Dark souls has that too, but the commitment of the basic attacks is crazy. The combo is 4 attacks, which last like 0.5s, 1s, 2s, 2s. The last ones are sooooo long. Specially the 3rd, which feels ridiculous. Then, since they don't interrupt when you try to dodge, there were a lot of times where I saw the opportunity to attack, and WHILE an attack animation was executed, the boss attacked me with a quick attack that came from nowhere. Even if you react, the character will dodge late, or not dodge at all -> hit and frustration received.
-- The game even has a mechanic where, if you have a focus point (which you earn landing hits), you can combo a strong attack during a normal attack combo, which prevents damage and has some special perks. Well, susprise: IT DOES NOT INTERRUPT THE NORMAL ATTACKS EITHER. You already have to time it well in order to work, but it has to be also timed to be used when a normal attack ends??? Just riddiculous. 
--Also, the charged attacks take so long to execute (~2s just to start, ~2s to execute with the standard pose), that lots of times even when saw the opportunity, while waiting for it to land, the boss had time to (take a cofee and) hit-interrupt me, making me lose the focus points and health.
-- Also, some special abilities take so long to execute too, so the same can happen. Even when apparently timed well, the boss may start an attack from nowhere and interrupt you, but here's worse, because you lose the magic AND te ability enters cooldown, even if it wasn't executed!
--Heck, even the pause button failed to work sometimes during fights!

- The sheer quantity of boss bullsh*t. Quick and strong attacks that didn't happen before (and of course interrupt you while tried to play the game), invisible barriers where the boss can randomly stay behind in critical moments, weird hitboxes, unnoticeable magic attacks that stun you, visual effects that prevent you from seeing what's going on, big performance issues that make you lose all responsivity, crazy camera which follows the jumpy boss making you lose orientation and sight of the boss, big ellusive boss that runs / flies all around, making you tediously follow them all over the place trying to land a hit, attacks that trigger a way too long mini-cinematic that can make you die from poison / burn while waiting for it to end, weird phases in which they make your abilies useless and divide your max stamina by 2, magics that, even if they land, the boss will insta-free from them for no reason, target lock making you attack a point of the boss where they take no damage... Believe me, I could continue, but I guess you get the idea. The game has lots of bosses, but they clearly prioritised quantity over quality.

- The last chapter felt so much like filler. Big empty map with lack of points of interest, with some bosses scattered here and there. Also, didn't know where to go to advance in the story at some point.

- There's so much detail in the environment that sometimes it lacks propper readability (Unreal 5 game).

- Secondary missions have no markers or way to know where they are, or at which progression point you are, or what you have to do with the items they give you. The way you start the dragons one is absurdly obscure.

- Lots of invisible walls. E.g. sometimes a cave will be explorable, sometimes it will be out of reach. No visual difference whatsoever.

- Total lack of weight in combat. No controller vibration.

- The story doesn't really care if you follow it or not. Rather, I had the sensation that it gives for granted that you already know the legend, as things just happen for no apparent reason, characters pop in and out, and the chapters just start at a different place with a different setting with no context whatsoever. Knowing more about the story of Journey to the West was one of my interests with this game, but more than a story this was more like... a summary? Didn't feel like reading the walls of text in the codex either, even less after seeing that most are just as obtuse as the rest of the narrative.


[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
Inevitably, after seeing the trailers and how pretty the game looked, I set my expectatives for it to be at the same level as its AAA counterparts. Unfortunately, even if the artistic part did well the job, in regard to gameplay and game feel the game fell short. And not only that, but found heaps of artificial difficulty (by design or not) in lots of bosses that made the experience frustrating and tedious. A real shame!

looks amazing. The visuals and art direction are easily its strongest point.

But the combat is boring. The weapon variety feels uninspired, damage feedback feels flat, and fights don’t evolve in interesting ways. After a while, everything starts to feel the same.

Boss design leans too heavily on size. Instead of making bosses mechanically impressive, the game just makes them huge. And when the camera can’t even handle those oversized fights properly, it becomes frustrating rather than epic. It feels like the game doesn’t know how to make bosses feel powerful, so it just scales them up.

In the end, Wukong is visually stunning — but mechanically shallow.

review_text:
Grand Theft Auto V  is still one of the best open-world games you can play. Developed by Rockstar Games, it offers a massive, detailed world (Los Santos) packed with missions, side activities, and chaos.

The single-player story follows three unique protagonists, each with their own personality and playstyle, which keeps the narrative fresh and engaging. The gameplay blends shooting, driving, flying, and exploration seamlessly. On PC, graphics settings allow for impressive visuals and smooth performance.

GTA Online adds huge replay value with heists, businesses, races, and frequent updates. However, new players may find the grind or in-game economy challenging without extra time investment.

⭐ Pros: Huge open world, engaging story, tons of content, strong modding community on PC.
⚠️ Cons: Online grind, occasional hackers in public lobbies.

Overall: A must-play open-world classic that still holds up incredibly well on Steam.

review_text:
Unturned was more than just a game for me. I started playing it back in the beta days, when it was simple, clean, and full of charm. The blocky graphics had personality, the survival gameplay was fun, and the game felt special. You could play for hours without getting bored, especially with friends. It didn’t need realism to be good — it was simply fun.

Up until around 2018, Unturned was an amazing game. The community felt more united, servers were full, and updates added content without ruining the core of the game. For me, it was the game of my childhood, full of great memories, late nights on classic maps, and moments that really mattered.

Sadly, after that period, things started to go downhill. Bad updates, unnecessary changes, and questionable decisions slowly pushed old players away. The community became more toxic, and the game lost its original direction. Even if the developer, Nelson, may have had good intentions, in my opinion the game was ruined by updates that no longer respected what made Unturned special.

Unturned will always have a place in my heart, but not for what it is today — for what it used to be. A simple, beautiful game that defined a part of my childhood and created memories I’ll never forget.

Unturned is a sleeper hit that really pulls you in. The crafting system is way deeper than it looks at first, and the open world? Packed with places to explore, loot to snag, and weird little surprises around every corner.

There’s a ton of stuff to gather and build with, so you can totally make your playstyle your own, whether you're going full survivalist, base-builder, or just roaming and causing chaos.

Multiplayer takes it to another level. You can team up with your buddies or go full rogue and mess with other players - either way, it keeps things fresh and wild.

With its super addictive loop and a community that’s always doing cool stuff, Unturned easily earns its spot as a must-try if you’re into survival games.

review_text:
Let's start with the visuals. Prepare to be amazed by the stunningly blocky graphics that would make Picasso question his artistic choices. It's like someone turned a potato into a pixelated masterpiece and ran with it. Who knew that a world full of squares and rectangles could be so captivating?

Now, don't let the charming art style fool you. The game packs a punch when it comes to challenges. From fending off brain-hungry zombies to scavenging for toilet paper (yes, even in the apocalypse, that's a thing), Unturned throws curveballs at you faster than a clumsy outfielder.

But fear not, for the game's survival mechanics are as easy to grasp as a greased pig. You'll quickly learn the art of crafting weapons out of unlikely objects, building fortresses that would make Tony Stark proud, and driving vehicles that handle like drunk shopping carts. It's a recipe for chaos, and it tastes oh-so-delicious.

The multiplayer aspect is where Unturned truly shines. Grab your friends and jump into the madness together. Team up to create the most absurd bases, engage in epic battles that resemble a circus on steroids, or embark on zany quests that make you question your life choices. It's the kind of multiplayer experience that leaves you crying tears of laughter and wondering why you didn't become a professional clown.

Unturned on Steam is a game that never takes itself seriously, and that's precisely why it's so damn fun. It's a wild rollercoaster ride through a blocky wonderland, where laughter is your best weapon and silliness is your survival strategy.

So, if you're looking for a game that will tickle your funny bone and make your friends question your sanity, look no further. Unturned is here to make you laugh, cry (from laughing too hard), and question why you ever took gaming so seriously in the first place. Embrace the absurdity and embark on this hilarious journey. Your inner comedian will thank you.

review_text:
I sank 10,000 hours into Lost Ark over three years. A lot of those hours is AFK while multi-task working from home. 

The combat is a literal 10/10 – the most fluid, responsive, and skill-expressive action combat ever shipped in an MMO. Every other system exists to gatekeep it.

To earn gold you raid.
You can only do a few raids each week per character.
There is no, "farming to make gold"
You make alts to do more raids, to make more gold.
To raid with pugs you need titles.
To earn titles you need gold → gear → engravings → gems high enough that party leaders actually accept you.
To become a party leader yourself you must have title, gear, engravings, and gems good enough for players to want to join you for the social proof. Then you also need to be able to lead the raid by running the sidereals. 

The loop is engineered to pressure Pay-to-Win from the in-game shop. RMT sites always stay one step ahead of bans, so most players I played with swiped that way. Credit-card swiping the cash shop is possible but hilariously inefficient. I watched players drop $50k only to see every single purchase handed out in a new-player pass six months later.

F2P route: maintain six alts, run every single raid on all of them, funnel 100 % of resources into one main. Miss a single week and your character falls behind the ilvl curve, groups won't accept you, and the cycle resets. 

I mained Pistoleer when it was universally called a troll spec. Built a partnered YouTube channel around raid nights and Pistoleer gameplay. The eventual buff felt like vindication toward the end before I quit playing.

The deeper problem is systemic burnout by design.

• Novelty-first philosophy: cutscenes and long animations you cannot skip after the first time.
• 12-month patch lag: community screams, developers “listen” exactly one year later.
• FOMO layered on FOMO: cash shop, title gates for pugs, new content dropped exclusively on holidays when normal humans are with family.

Every design decision screams “make it fresh for the first playthrough, make it painful for the 999th.” Replayability was never the goal; retention-through-grind was.

Take Lost Ark’s combat, drop it into a League-of-Legends-story arch & universe that rewards replayability, removes all P2W vectors, and you would have the greatest MMORPG ever made.

What we actually have is a Korean grind factory with god-tier raids and the single best combat engine in the genre, deliberately crippled by monetization, title politics, and anti-replayability systems. Every decision they make feels out of touch, and makes you wonder if anyone designing the game actually plays the game. Also, the stories and scripts are 100% done by AI.

Combat: 10/10.
Everything else: designed to make you quit so they can sell you the solution.

review_text:
Pros: As a free to play game Lost Ark is good. If you like a Diablo-like birds-eye view hack and slash game it is also top tier. The main draw of Lost Ark comes from its boss fights. The boss fights are unlike any other MMO I've played. The story is good or can be skipped with the crtl+g mechanic. Recently Lost Ark has made steps in allowing people to play raids solo as of this review it is 1680 item level and below. That is every raid in the game except the last 2. Lost Ark provides plenty of oppurtunities to power level characters to help get newer players into the end game. As of writing they are currently giving a powerpass, which automatically catches you're character up into the story and gives them appropriate gear ie 1640 for tier 4. Next they give you a power pass which boosts honing success rates, decreases honing costs, and gives free items to help the honing processes.

Cons: As a free to play game Lost Ark needs to make money somehow. First things first Lost Ark is pay to win. The top players can buy materials to hone and upgrade their characters using the in-game item shops and gold. Next is the RNG factor that comes with upgrading characters and honing. Every possible upgrade is made through an RNG system. Honing is not as bad as BDO's was but it is still miserable. Ex. you get 28,000 gold for doing the 1680 raid solo. Each chance of honing has to upgrade your armor from 1680 to 1685 has a 5% chance to succeed and costs around 2,000 gold per attempt. This is one of the largest downsides of Lost Ark as more senior players will tell you more details about how their journey went. BY FAR THE WORST PART IS THE RAID GATEKEEPING. For the last couple of raids you'd need to find a raid group. You'll see terms like prog, homework, and very occasionally learning. The only chance you'd have to get in one of these raids groups is to find or create you're own learning raid and do this 10 times, for 10 weeks or so to get the title which will allow you to participate in the hw raids and sometimes prog raids. 

My verdict as a free to play player; I would suggest playing lost ark if you like playing cool boss fights and number go up style of satisfaction. The first time you'd hit 1,000,000 is a great feeling. However, playing during events is heavily recommended.

review_text:
10% of this game: The most brilliant and dopamine fueled class, combat, and boss design I've ever experienced in any video game ever.
90% of this game: Degrading busywork, abusive RNG progression, absurd menu bloat, and overpriced microtransactions.

The above facts are mentally and emotionally inescapable. I thought about it every time I wasted hours getting trapped in a raid through no fault of my own on a weekly basis; every time I threw away weeks worth of gold and materials on failed progression attempts; every time my interest in a new class release was repressed by the realization that I didn't even have time to play the existing ones; every time my hope and excitement for a new boss was crushed by the math showing that the rewards would not offset the progression and opportunity cost of accessing that boss until after 6-12 months of repeating it weekly.

Equalized content used to be the way to enjoy the 10% without subjecting yourself to the 90%, but the developers have removed it with no announced plans to replace it, and all of their recent efforts indicate that they never will. After quitting cold turkey over a year ago, I decided to give it another try with the recent anniversary event, and I could not put up with it for more than one day. For the first time in years I saw the game through the lens of a new player and it's truly repulsive. Even with my years of knowledge, experience, progress, achievements, and accumulated wealth worth literally thousands of dollars, I couldn't bring myself to chase the now rotten carrot on the stick. Best of luck to any new players starting with nothing.

Ok so imma finally gonna leave a review. I'm a returning player that has played since alpha. 

This is what I think of the state of the game:

For a new player that's never played a Korean MMO, its grindy and has RNG systems for progressing. It has p2w leaned mechanics for end game. Not necessary but will get u there faster.

If that's a pass in your book, try the game. You're given power passes (every release of a new class) which boost your level up to (currently tier 4) skipping all old content. 
If you start fresh, you'll most likely have to do all old raids for progression solo and imo can be a rough experience especially the current T3 honing currency.
 Its still required gold instead of silver. We are supposed to get an update soon.
 (As of 2/4 this change has been implemented.)  

With Guardian Knight (the newest class) being released in Feb 2026 there will be a new power pass.

With that being said, its a pretty game with unique classes. Designed with Unreal engine 3.
Director said they will not upgrade and keep this engine.

Amazon Game Studio is the publisher and I can tell you from experience that the customer service is horrid.
Don't expect them to help you recover anything over a month ago. Customer Service Representative told me they only keep purchasing records for a month. (on a long break i lost most skins, including my founders skin and mount)

I'm an MMO veteran and can say the true action combat system and raids so far have been the best experience I've had so far within the genre. 

Feel free to ask any questions and/or if your looking for learners raids (for current content) on NA.

Hope this review helps you make your decision. We'd love to have you!

review_text:
tl;dr: Temper your expectations. Devs will never stop adding vertical progression systems. FOMO will be the end of you. If you do not have an active guild, static, or are not on a Discord server that organizes raids, you're going to have a very bad time. Alternatively, pay ~$100k USD to immediately max your character out.

I wish there was a "Neutral" option instead of straight up having to recommend or not recommend a game. At it's core, Lost Ark is a fantastic isometric ARPG with some of the best combat, boss design, and raids in the genre. Of course, this is a Korean MMO, so you have two options if you want to be viable in endgame raids (which are the main selling point and attractions of the game). You can either shell out a ridiculous amount of money in order to bypass the relentless, nonstop grind for character power, or you can play this game like a second job, raiding on multiple characters on multiple rosters in order to maybe be strong enough to be accepted into endgame raids. There is also a third, less popular option that I recommend, which is to not give in to FOMO and simply play at your own pace. 

Lost Ark is the definition of a "marathon, not a sprint" game. The devs here are not completely clueless (unlike some other KRMMOs *cough* Blade & Soul *cough*) and frequently host catch-up events that new players can take advantage of to quickly and relatively painlessly progress to almost endgame levels. 

However, this only shifts the problem from being eligible for participating in endgame raids to having nobody accept you for raids because people can easily tell from a glance if you are new to the game (low roster level is an immediate giveaway, not having requisite achievements that can only be gotten from playing the raids you are trying to apply to is also a giveaway). Truly, the only way a new player will be accepted into raids is if you go out of your way to find a static, guild, or join a community Discord that organizes raids. Pugging will absolutely destroy your sanity, and carries the extreme risk of being "jailed" in raids (the game will only let you progress through gates in a raid with people with the same gate completion, so if your party disbands mid-raid, you are SoL).

All in all, if you have a static, friends to play with, or are in a Discord that organizes raids, then you'll probably have a great time with this game. If you're a solo player that wants to experience the endgame, you probably won't have trouble getting to endgame due to the existence of solo raids, but you are going to have a VERY bad time in party finder trying to persuade pugs to let you join them. 

Some other things to note for prospective players that don't quite fit anywhere else in this review: 

(1) Classes are gender-locked - this might be a dealbreaker for a lot of people - and there is a strong bias towards female classes. 
(2) Raids are limited entry - you can only enter a raid once per character per week, and you can only enter 3 different raids per character per week. Meaning you will have to play alts if you want to make any meaningful income.
(3) Raids are difficult, and personal responsibility is high - a single person can wipe the entire raid with certain mechanics, and it is expected that you study raid guides thoroughly before joining raids. Some of these guides can be hours long. Expect to prog for dozens of hours on endgame raids if you have no experience.
(4) RNG upon RNG upon RNG - upgrading ANYTHING involves copious amounts of RNG. You WILL get frustrated with honing and rolling for stats and lines on accessoires. On the flipside, you CAN get lucky and save millions of gold with a lucky tap or roll.
(5) There is a story. Is it good? Eh. Is it voiced? Sometimes? Should you care about it? Maybe, if you're into it. Don't expect something magnificent is what I'm getting at.

Solid 5/10 game. Would've been great if it wasn't a KRMMO.

review_text:
It's a horrible shame there is no other game that plays identical to Lost Ark because it is truly among my absolute favorite combat designs I've ever played. Sadly many aspects of the game that cannot be ignored represent enormous barriers to most of the enjoyment the game has in store.

I knew many months ago that I was reaching my personal stopping point after playing every week since launch. There are only so many thorns I can step on before I can no longer walk. Those thorns include fomo, homework, gatekeeping, pay-to-win, luck disparity/bad luck protection, miserable progression systems, progression behind time gates, progression that requires unrelated collectible farming, rampant bots, rampant RMT, and either sweats or imposters sucking the fun out of practically every raid that you don't do purely with your close friends/static raid group. And even then, even the tightest of groups seem to fall apart seemingly at random due to some level of drama or miscommunication. I'm quite happy ditching what felt to me like a community of adult children, but mileage may vary.

Absolutely do not play Lost Ark. What enjoyment it can bring you will be overshadowed by how long you will spend waiting for that enjoyment, and with every update; the new-player experience is made worse.

review_text:
I’ve been playing Lost Ark since the Western beta. At the time, I was working at Amazon in the IT department and wanted to be part of something different outside of my 9–5. I played the game pre-release and post-release, and in the beginning it genuinely felt exciting and fun.

Progressing through the story, exploring the world, and learning the systems was enjoyable—especially because I was playing alongside my best friend. Early on, the game felt rewarding and social, and there was a real sense of momentum as you moved forward.

However, once progression became heavily tied to gear honing, resource grinding, and item level requirements, the experience changed completely. The grind to increase item level became incredibly frustrating and time-consuming, to the point where it felt almost impossible without extreme dedication or spending. This is ultimately what caused my best friend to stop playing altogether.

On top of that, gatekeeping became a major issue. Endgame content increasingly revolves around strict requirements—high item levels, perfect engravings, optimal card sets, and specific classes—making it extremely difficult for returning, casual, or unlucky players to participate. Even when you meet the basic requirements, it’s common to be declined repeatedly from groups unless you vastly overgear the content.

This creates a cycle where:

You need raids to progress

But you can’t get into raids without already being over-progressed

Which pushes players toward burnout, bussing, or quitting entirely

I continued playing for longer—partly due to my connection with the company—but over time it became clear that Lost Ark feels less like a game and more like a second job. Daily chores, time-gated content, and FOMO-driven systems don’t respect the player’s time, especially for anyone with real-life responsibilities.

This sentiment is widely shared in the community. While Lost Ark has excellent combat, beautiful visuals, and some of the best raid designs in the genre, it relies heavily on:

Excessive daily and weekly homework

RNG-based progression that can feel punishing

A gatekeeping-heavy endgame culture that discourages new or returning players

Eventually, burnout becomes inevitable.

Now, I mostly log in only for new content, events, or free rewards, rather than playing consistently. The core gameplay is still impressive, but the overall progression and social systems make it hard to enjoy long-term unless the game becomes your main focus.

Lost Ark is a great game at its core—but one that struggles to balance ambition, accessibility, and community health. If you have unlimited time, you may love it. If not, it can quickly become exhausting.

review_text: Basically, the game is really fun. The story is cool, the skills are flashy, there's lots of side content, and the dungeons are challenging. But here's the problem. After 400 hours, I've played 95% of the game alone. There are virtually no players in T3, and it's designed so that you can play it alone because the developers know that you're completely on your own. I thought it would be better in T4 because it's “presumably” end-game content. Even there, I can't find any people, and if there is a party, you have to wait forever. I only see parties for end-end-game content, but until then, it's NOT an MMORPG just because you see some people in towns. And now comes the worst part: from T4 onwards, you realize that progress becomes difficult without the cash shop. I have nothing against progress becoming more difficult, but I haven't found a way to grind. All you can do are dailies and weeklies. And if you have to spend $500+ a month to get “the experience,” then it ultimately leads to Lost Ark being a mobile MMORPG light.

review_text:
Fun game if you played since launch. Great combat. But I can't in good faith recommend starting to play it.

Worst new player experience in existence. Due to weekly lockouts, you will spend months soloing content nobody runs anymore before catching up to current endgame, where you will be gatekept - because game strongly encourages running 3 raids per week on 6 chars, people want fast clears and won't risk taking someone inexperienced as they really want their 18 weekly raids to take 30 minutes each rather than 3 hours each. If you endure, after a few months you can catch up, somewhat. You can also swipe to skip the grind, but being gatekept for no experience will still apply.

Game is pay to win in the sense that it enables cash to in-game currency exchange. There's technically no advantage over other players that can be obtained exclusively by swiping, but paying enough can skip literal years of grinding, making you relatively stronger than players who spent less.

In short, game with amazing combat, great story - but badly translated and with mixed quality of voice acting, awful progression and equally bad, actively hostile new player experience.

review_text:
I will leave you my few cents regarding lostark, as someone with over 9k hours in the game for the past 3 years, think i can pretty much tell you the reason why you SHOULD and SHOULDN'T play this game at all.

So for the SHOULD:

Are you unemployed or rich? then definitely this might be the game for you, as it currently stands for a ready to raid player, you will be needing either a lot of time to catch up, or spend more than 5K USD on RMT to have your basic stuff ready for it.
Do you enjoy combat with great feel design? then again this game is definitely for you, LostArk biggest strength lies on it's combat feel.

Now for the SHOULDN'T:
If you are someone who is not prepared to be put through long playing time because either there is someone who is messing up a lot with late raids, then yeah expect to lose a lot of time in pulls
If you are someone who gets frustated because the class you picked up is doing poorly, then again you are out of luck, smilegate(the developer) has been pretty bad at balancing older classes vs newly released ones
Are you familiar with WOW fomo systems? then be prepared that every new raid might introduce a new GOLD SINK and a NEW PROGRESSION system
Are you someone who enjoys having to get your feedback ignored? Then be prepared, while AMAZON does a good job at compiling a lot of the feedback, the sad reality is that it gets ignored by SMILEGATE.
Are you someone who wants to min-max? Well that's too bad because SMILEGATE doesn't like it that you can min max your build or char, there is always a need to keep you running on the wheel
You like raiding a lot? Well good news, currently you can do up to 18 raids a week between 6 CHARACTERS
Oh also i forgot, unless you are putting some $$$ into the game, then you must be mindful on your investment into your characters too, hence those 18 raids a week done might be done for you to funnel a character into a hard raid status raid ready while the rest rots in the bottom.

While Lostark has creative raid and combat designs, it is constantly constrained and weighted down by many of the system designs that Smilegate wants to push forward, there is no denying in the potential that the game could have, is still there, locked behind an incompetent developer that listens to whales first rather than the casual player
Yes there are still express events that will let you raise 1 character to a playable status but this won't be enough for you to feel at an okay pace to play the game, my honest opinion is that really there are better things to do, learn a language, workout more, or other useful things, LOSTARK is not a game you want to currently play unless you can ignore all the SHOULDN'T and can be okay with the SHOULD to play it.

So yeah that's it folks, if you play and don't want to stress, make 6 valkyries and go full support or 6 bards too, then you have boobs and not so rough time.

So yeah imma go keep playing more WH40k Rogue trader
Cheers

review_text:
Tbh, it’s one of the games with the best combat feel I’ve ever played. Especially when Slayer came out the character’s skills and sword were so satisfying that I could’ve turned all my alts into Slayers. But after a certain point, the game became unplayable because of gatekeeping. I quit about two years ago, but I wanted to come back and take a look.

But what I saw was the same thing again. The game was full of bots. When I last quit, it was pay-to-win, but now it has basically become pay-to-play. You literally can’t move without spending money. And you’re still forced to do your dailies with every character like some kind of slave. I don’t understand how a company can ignore its players this much. Even putting that aside, why are the bosses still so punishing? With this much gatekeeping and such a solid foundation for a great game, why not just make the game actually playable?

I mean, you can’t even find a group for the bosses you need to fight every week to upgrade certain items, sometimes spending hours, days, or even weeks trying. Some people just quit in the later stages because they don’t want to bother. The old raid is meaningless, the gameplay feels pointless. The sense of progression drops so much after a certain gear score that I can’t even find a single reason to keep playing this game.

Honestly, it’s one of the rare games with really great level and combat design in my eyes, but I think it will shut down eventually like New World, so I’d say don’t bother at all. Especially expecting anything reasonable from these developers is more pointless than just sitting at home and waiting for your GPU to evolve itself.

review_text:
Hello, non-Steam War Thunder player here with 3,500 hours on file.
Pros: tanks look cool
Cons: Numerous and varied.
- The current server architecture is absolutely unstable at an inherently painful level. Movement issues, input lag, random server spikes across the board (that the entire server talks about in chat for 5 laggy, painful minutes), the ancient GHOST SHELL BUG, feature of multiple 'ITS FIXED!' reports (no it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ isn't) and now a litany of stupid microjitters AND/OR invisible solid objects on maps which are just oh, so fun to drive into. Oh, and the lack of an Australian server (South Asia Ping? 180 if you're lucky. Packet loss? 10% minimum at peak times), but that's a personal peeve.

- Gaijin cannot possibly fathom the concept of gameplay innovation. If they'd instead consider the homeless man outside their offices, bashing away with a dustbin lid, this might change, because there are very, very few gamemodes actually populated beyond the basic 4; because those gamemodes outside the basic 4, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck, because they're 'unpopulated' and 'nobody plays those, so why would we innovate on them and introduce fun new mechanics? Nah, add dozer blades to like a dozen tanks instead.' Those basic 4 are also extremely boring. Air Realistic is completely unplayable for bombers above 9.0, nullifying massive swathes of playable aircraft and relegating them to the bin, Ground Realistic is an exercise in not being hit by an exorbitantly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ projectile that violated several laws of the games' physics engine in order to save server performance and Arcade is effectively the only playable, enjoyable game mode - that doesn't give you enough progression to warrant playing it, because the length of time to grind above 5.0 is, funnily enough, reminiscent of a snail's pace.

- Predatory marketing taken to notable extremes. Do you want to progress in this game? Your time-to-grind will be more than halved with a Premium account. Premium account promotions are shovelled absolutely anywhere they can be. And it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ expensive, even OFF the Steam branch of this game (which incurs additional fees) the purchasable currency, advancements, premium account, etc etc, are all ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane expensive. Oh, AND, $120 AUD for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ F/A-18? Seriously? Or a Leopard 2A-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? Or a boat? $120? I shamefully admit I've thrown a disgusting amount of money at this game but I must admit, I regret those purchases and the support for this company resultant. No more.

I strongly advise against picking this up. Go elsewhere, like MTC4 on Roblox, or GHPC once it shows promise.

review_text:
This game is the living embodiment of an abusive relationship. The map design is by far some of the worst I've ever seen, on some maps it's so bad that if you get a specific spawn you may as well just leave as you will be spawn sniped in ~2 minutes. Rather than balance things properly Gajin will randomly nerf tanks making them non-historic. HSTVLs round underperforming despite hundreds of bug reports with official government docs as sources, no change is made. The games volumetric penetration simulation is jank at its absolute best, roof MG’s eating 500lb bombs, headlights tanking APDS, and 35mm APHE oneshotting T-72’s head on. Gajin refuses to decompress the BR’s causing vehicles to either be unusable or completely unfair to fight entirely on RNG. 

  The game is free to play IF, you are a very competent player maintaining a high positive K/D 99% of the time. With the above issues this is nigh impossible. Premium vehicles are overpriced and then some, and in most cases straight up pay to win. With an unbearably long grind to Top tier many players buying top tier tanks, being out matched then leaving after one death leading to some teams rushing head-on with no idea of what they were doing getting killed and leaving the rest of the team to pick up the slack. Sometimes over half your team are these people.

CAS is a plague on the game, 1 assist and there's a fully loaded Apache launching a half dozen Hellfires at your team with no ability to counter it.

But the game, despite its major flaws, is really fun! Every kill, every objective, every round tanked is a rush. There are very close games, or moments where you feel unstoppable. There are also moments where you go 0-5 with 1 assist for 4 games in a row. The grind wearing you down the longer you go. 

While I cannot in good faith recommend the game in its current state, it is fun sometimes. If you do play, be willing to put up with BS and have some disposable income to make the grind almost tolerable.

review_text:
This game is free to play but very pay to win. There is no option for  ground forces only , every ground battle is subjected to fighter and bomber destroying ground forces with no risk to the pilots of the planes. Plane deaths do not affect the spawn lives of players, die in a plane but still have same number of respawns prior to death.Very low rewards for shooting down aircraft compared to the difficulty in doing so. I have over 3,000 aircraft kills with spaa , tanks and tank destroyers more than 12,000 enemy kills and am at level 81. This game could be so much more however the developers seem reluctant to listen to player reviews. If you like to be killed by aircraft that you dont know are in the combat zone or destroyed by premium vehicles bought for real wold money, matched up against overpowered enemy nerfed if you dont renew a premium account [suddenly not able to damage other vehicles that usually  are destroyable by your vehicle . Any form of complaint are defended by ' just get better' . There are other ground force games on the way without aircraft or buy to win options , as soon as one emerges I wont be playing War Thunder untill then Im hooked.
Take my advise do not play War Thunder.

review_text:
Lack of content on launch, performance/server issues, annoying grind at times, but overall a wonderful experience that deserves to be tried out after its numerous updates. While not as difficult as older titles, I like to think of this game as a homage to Portable 3rd where you just hunt and vibe. 

The transmog system is so simple, I love to fashion hunt. I also love to catch and discover new species, soaking up the atmosphere of every environment. Although the maps are large, which can make the hunt feel drawn out, it feels relatively easy to stock up and travel, and experiment with different weapons if you're a new gen.

If you're not a fan of World or Rise, probably skip this one, either wise, enjoy your hunts!

review_text:
I’ve been playing Monster Hunter Wilds since release, and honestly, it’s been a ride. At launch, the game was gorgeous but super demanding — my old rig with an RTX 3070 could barely push 30 FPS. I ended up upgrading my PC just to enjoy it properly, and I’m glad I did because the visuals are stunning.

The early game felt pretty easy, and compared to Monster Hunter: World, the weapon and armor skills seemed limited. But I figured that was just because it was the start of the game. What really blew me away was the aesthetics — every map is beautiful, and the customization options are insane. You can tweak your hunter, your Seikrets, camps, even NPCs. It makes the world feel alive and personal.

Fast forward a year, and the game has improved a ton. Performance is way better (I’d say 20–26% smoother than launch), and the gameplay has gotten harder thanks to new monsters and events. Hunts feel more intense now, and I love that challenge. The best part is how the devs are clearly listening to feedback. They’ve been refining the game nonstop, and it shows. Credit where credit’s due — Capcom nailed the updates.

Now I’m just hyped for the upcoming DLC. If it keeps up the same level of polish and improvement, this game could easily surpass World in the long run.

review_text:
[h1]Monster Hunter Wilds TU4.5 Review[/h1]

[b]TLDR:[/b] It has been a year since its release, and the game is great and now highly playable. There is so much content you can do in the game. Even if you are new to the series or a veteran try it out. If you played during launch and dropped it because of the performance issues give it a second chance because you might really like it now.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Introduction & The State of the Game[/h2]
* [b]The Performance Turnaround:[/b] Launch performance was completely abysmal and left a horrible taste in many players mouths. It really should have been in a good state from the beginning. Thankfully after multiple optimization updates leading up to TU4.5 I can finally say the game runs smoothly and is very playable now.
* [b]Value:[/b] The content is so abundant it is almost overwhelming. No matter what price you buy this game at it is an absolute bang for your buck.

[h2]The Good: Combat, Monsters, and Story[/h2]
* [b]The MH Identity & Combat:[/b] The core gameplay has changed so much since MHP3rd but the overall combat is still as satisfying as ever. Optimized gameplay is buttery smooth and the combat is chef's kiss. It is a great evolution for the traditional MH Hack&Slash. Some veteran purists might prefer the original pacing and combo commitment but all I can say is try it and if it clicks then great.
* [b]Phenomenal Music:[/b] The music is phenomenal and fits every situation and environment. The music for each major monster is different and unique making it quite the spectacle.
* [b]Monster Roster & Story:[/b] The roster has amazing variety making it incredibly fun to fight new and returning monsters. The harder endgame bosses are just PEAK—wonderful cinematic and challenging fights blending set pieces and raw gameplay. There is more story now to progress the narrative and introduce the roster, and older fans will definitely love the characterization of returning characters.

[h2]Hunters, Gear, & QoL[/h2]
* [b]The Core Loop & Grind:[/b] The core loop of hunting monsters is satisfying and the endgame respects your time. You can avoid the RNG gear mechanics entirely and still clear the game. The base craftable Artian set and craftable charms are great upgrades if you do not want to farm for god roll talismans. Grinding for perfect stats is not for everyone but it is still a fun goal.
* [b]Equipment Freedom:[/b] There is so much cosplay and cool fashion available. It is a great blend of cool, cute, and silly/funny perfect for different tastes. Color customization is flexible and you are no longer restricted by gendered armor sets. If you want a fully armored gal or a sexy muscle man now you can.
* [b]Character Customization:[/b] The creator is incredibly detailed for making characters from fiction or reality. Even if you are not creative you can just search online for peoples character codes.
* [b]Support & QoL:[/b] You can have NPC support hunters help in battle and their carts do not count towards the quest failure. QoL changes make gameplay less tedious like easily reposting quests. Some might be divided on changes like Focus strike. Some love that you can adjust yourself during combos while others don't like it because it makes it easier to fight monsters.
* [b]Bonus Charm:[/b] The devs added small hidden things like the grandhub diva who gives a small buff after her performance or the secret bird's nest on the grandhub that gives you stuff from time to time.

[h2]The Bad: UI/UX, Network, & Nitpicks[/h2]
* [b]UI/UX Negative:[/b] The menus are confusing to navigate. It might be a skill issue in navigating the ancient forest on my part but it needs a touch up to be more digestible.
* [b]Cluttered Pop ups:[/b] Notification messages are messy. I want to know if I have a specific buff activated but it gets convoluted by notifications for things I don't care about right now. A filter would be great.
* [b]Default Controls:[/b] The default auto run for the Seikret and radial pop up for items feel clunky and need changing. Sometimes you do not even know there are much better settings because the UI/UX is convoluted, and I only knew about it because of youtube shorts on my feed. 
* [b]Investigation Quests:[/b] Great for saving world encounters but the limit of 50 is too small. Getting other players quests is pure RNG making it hard to get specific duo monster arena fights that you want to get. I hope we get a Custom Quest Maker.
* [b]Gathering and Delivery Quests:[/b] These shouldn't have been mostly removed as they gave players a breather to enjoy the environments. MHRise style event quests exploring the map would give more excuses to go straight from the Windward Plains to the Scarlet Forest without needing to fast travel.
* [b]Network Issues:[/b] I am not sure if it is because of crossplay or just server stability but I sometimes get disconnected suddenly leading to carts. We have decent internet and this doesn't happen in other games.
* [b]Missing Personal Rooms:[/b] I loved room customization in MHWorld and MHRise. Now it sucks that catching rare endemic life is just a number and a picture on my profile instead of something to display.

[h2]The Ugly: DLC & Monetization[/h2]
* [b]Overpriced DLC:[/b] Optional cosmetics are great but prices are a bit much. It also did not help that cosmetic DLC were released before the optimization updates which annoyed a lot of people.
* [b]Lore Behind Paywalls:[/b] Items like Alma's table give unique lore dialogue. It sucks that you have to pay to learn this lore. The basic version should have been free.
* [b]Character Edit Vouchers:[/b] Limiting edits to a maximum of 3 times and hiding further changes behind a paywall is very scummy. This should have been a completely free feature.

[hr][/hr]

[b]The Ultimate Verdict:[/b] Despite the issues and nitpicks I have this is a wonderful experience to pick up. Monster Hunter Wilds is a great game held back due to its rough performance and available content on release. The game was clearly rushed but as you can see with the constant updates the devs poured a lot of care and passion into this game. This is my biased view as a fan of this series since I was a kid, but I encourage you to try out the game. If you dropped it during launch because of the performance issues give it another chance to shine as you might just really enjoy it now.

review_text:
It's more monster hunter.... but is it? The main story questline is pretty easy, so you rush straight through to high rank. You might get stuck and need to hunt a previous monster a couple of times to craft armor with poison or fire resistance ONCE or twice, then you'll get through.

Then once you get to high rank the progression system changes and you don't care about hunting specific monsters anymore. You craft the best weapons from "broken blade" and "cracked tube" or whatever. Not from monster teeth. So the Carve, Craft, Repeat loop is gone.

Plus the fake Guardian monsters are not part of the ecosystem which feels lame.

The game is pretty, the combat is fun, but imo they're close to forgetting what makes monster hunter special.

review_text:
I have played every Monster Hunter games since tri. I love Monster Hunter games, I love the challenge, I love seeing the monsters "live" in the enviroments, I love the weapons and the combat, the cooking, the online community. We had wholesome and hard hunts in mh4u, even when none of us could talk to eachother, cause no one in the lobby could speak english.

MH: Wilds is by far the worst and least enjoyable MH game I have ever played. MH: Online was better than this, And I can't read chinese. I didn't know what was happening half the time.

The combat is great. IMO the graphics are really nice. I think the Seikret is a good addition and the areas are great.

But this is not a true MH game. It feels like Final Fantasy, painted in MH colours. I don't want to disable items, I want to throw them out of the inventory! The story is incredibly annoying. We lost the MH language and the palico can SHUT UP for all I care.
And the worst of it is the Gogamizos fight. It's an easy battle, but the dps check is completely unnecessary. Yes, we had DPS checks in all games. Yes its an established thing in the MH games, but it was always something special. In mh4u, you could at least scale the walls during the ultimate attack, you got cannons and railways and it felt like something was at stake.

And worst of all, this game runs badly. If you want an MH game to play, go play World.

review_text: Fun when it first came out, but many design oversights have led to the devs putting bandaids on a lot of different systems which ultimately remove agency from the player. The lack of follow-through on any promises to make things better is the nail in the coffin for me, they have been promising better communication and a focus on bug fixes for the better part of a year, and not a single thing has actually been done since those public statements were made. If the devs had any interest in expanding the game outside of bimonthly microtransaction packs and weekly filler events, they would have done it at some point in the past two years. I think the game became more popular than the devs expected, and it honestly feels like they are trying to ween off a large portion of the player base rather than rise to meet expectations. If the devs reasonably follow through on any of the promises they have made to date, I'll change my review to reflect that, but for now, my review is based on disappointment and the valley between what we have and what could have been.

Anyone wants a 4 player team game that is fun I cant recommend this game enough.

On the downside, if a toxic player hasn't connected a psn account the report button LITERALLY does nothing. And I mean NOTHING.
